# accmeta

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/giuseppealfonzetti/accmeta/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/giuseppealfonzetti/accmeta/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

Penalised estimation of meta-analysis models for diagnostic accuracy, in terms of sensitivity and specificity (bivariate model) or sensitivity, specificity and prevalence (trivariate model), combining cohort and case-control studies. Three estimators are available: a linear mixed model
(LMM) using a within-study normal approximation, the
generalized linear mixed model (GLMM), and an iterative bootstrap (IB) that corrects
the bias of the LMM by simulating from the GLMM. All are fitted through `fit_meta_model()`, with the estimator's options set by `set_control()`. IB fits come with a
covariance matrix and Wald or basic confidence intervals, built from a simulated
Jacobian of the TGLMM score.

## Installation

You can install the package via 

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pak::pkg_install("giuseppealfonzetti/accmeta")
```

## Example

Setup true parameter value

```{r truepar}
library(accmeta)

th <- c(2.94, -2.2, -0.4, 0.0953, 0.4, -0.5108, 0.3, 0.2, -0.6931)
theta2list(th)
min(eigen(theta2list(th)$SIGMA)$values)

```

Simulate data from true model

```{r data}
set.seed(1)
x <- sim_data(15, th, sample(40:200, 15, TRUE))
head(x)
```

Counts go in through `set_meta_data()`, which checks them and computes the
summaries the models need. 

```{r meta}
d <- set_meta_data(x)
d
```

A continuity correction is needed by the approximate
model whenever a cell is empty. You can use the CC argument:

```{r}
d_cc <- set_meta_data(x, CC = 0.5)
d_cc
```


Now we can fit the models. Note that the TGLMM can be directly fitted on the original data.

```{r fits}
tlmm <- fit_meta_model(d_cc, MODEL = "trivariate", ESTIMATOR = "lmm")
tglmm <- fit_meta_model(d, MODEL = "trivariate", ESTIMATOR = "glmm")
ib <- fit_meta_model(d_cc, MODEL = "trivariate", ESTIMATOR = "ib")
ib
```

`coef()` extract estimated parameters:

```{r coef}
coef(tlmm)
coef(tglmm)
coef(ib)

```

All models are estimated, by default, with the recommended Wishart prior, whose `DEGREES = NULL` means $p + 2$ for $p$ random effects. You can change it via

```{r}
tglmm_mle <- fit_meta_model(
  d,
  MODEL = "trivariate",
  ESTIMATOR = "glmm",
  PRIOR = set_prior(DEGREES = 4, SCALE = Inf)
)
coef(tglmm_mle)
min(eigen(coef(tglmm_mle)$SIGMA)$values)
min(eigen(coef(tglmm)$SIGMA)$values)

```


## Inference for the IB estimate

With `VCOV = TRUE` in `set_control()`, the IB also computes the Jacobian at the estimate.  `NCORES` spreads both the
simulated fits of each iteration and the Jacobian draws for parallel computations
```{r ib-vcov}
ib <- fit_meta_model(
  d_cc,
  MODEL = "trivariate",
  ESTIMATOR = "ib",
  CONTROL = set_control("ib", VCOV = TRUE, NCORES = 4)
)
```

`update(ib, VCOV = TRUE)` adds the Jacobian to an existing fit, using the fit's `CONTROL`.
`vcov()` and `confint()` work in the working coordinates of the IB, i.e the means, the log
standard deviations and the Fisher-z partial correlations.

```{r ib-ci}
sqrt(diag(vcov(ib)))
confint(ib)
confint(ib, METHOD = "basic")
```

Intervals mapped onto the natural scale via

```{r ib-natural}
confint(ib, SCALE = "natural")
```

Intervals mapped onto the reporting scale via

```{r ib-reporting}
confint(ib, SCALE = "reporting")
```
